Six days ago, Apple released iOS 27.2 developer beta 1, skipping iOS 27.1 beta. After releasing developer beta 2 yesterday, Apple has now launched the first public beta of iOS 27.2, which includes a brand-new iPhone Health app. Apple has also enabled the feature to book and purchase lab services through Quest Diagnostics in the new Health app version, applicable to iOS 27.2 beta.

iOS 27.2 beta includes a brand-new Health app and more features

iOS 27.2 is the version following iOS 27, which was officially released on September 14. iOS 27.1 is only available for iPhone Duo.

Apple has previously detailed how the iOS 27.1 SDK will allow developers to take full advantage of the iPhone Duo's display. You can check here how apps developed for different iOS versions display on the iPhone Duo.

Apple released Xcode 27.1 beta on Friday, adding iPhone Duo simulator and support for app development on the all-new foldable iPhone.

The first iOS 27.2 developer beta includes the following updates:

  • The redesigned Health app, first announced by Apple at the iPhone 18 Pro launch event, has officially arrived in this beta version.
  • Group FaceTime adds a dual-camera simultaneous shooting mode.
  • Siri AI language support now adds French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish.
  • Apple TV app profile feature lands on iPhone.
  • In Apple Podcasts, "Up Next" has been changed to "Latest Episode", while the "Continue Playing" section is placed directly below "Latest Episode". The Podcasts episode list also uses a background colour matched to the show's colour.
  • Apple Music now uses fewer icon colours as label colours in the app.

iOS 27.2 is expected to be officially released in October. iPhone users can currently try out the new Apple Health app in advance through the developer beta or public beta channels.
